module_description: get_model_response() in src/model_client.py, the core function that sends a prompt to Gemini and returns the text response, with retry logic on server errors.
requirements_excerpt: Source: src/model_client.py, docstring for get_model_response() (lines ~90-115). "On failure (rate limit, bad key, network issue, etc.), this retries a small number of times with a short pause, then raises ModelCallError with a clear message instead of letting the raw SDK traceback crash the whole script." Retry uses exponential backoff (2s, 4s, ...) up to max_retries (default 2, so 3 attempts total).
expected_behaviour: At least 3 grounded test cases, each citing this excerpt. Expected coverage: (1) a successful call on the first attempt returns the text response, (2) a ServerError on attempt 1 followed by success on attempt 2 still returns the response after a retry, (3) ServerError on every attempt raises ModelCallError once max_retries is exhausted. No invented behaviour beyond what the excerpt states.

module_description: _log_call() in src/model_client.py, the helper that writes a JSONL trace record for every model call.
requirements_excerpt: Source: src/model_client.py, docstring for get_model_response() (lines ~95-100). "Every call — successful or failed — is logged to evidence/traces/ with a timestamp, the prompt version label, the full prompt sent, and either the response or the error. This is the evidence trail required by the project brief (US-10)."
expected_behaviour: At least 3 grounded test cases, each citing this excerpt. Expected coverage: (1) a successful call writes a record with status 'success', a populated response field, and error None, (2) a failed call writes a record with status 'failed', response None, and a populated error field, (3) the trace file is written under evidence/traces/ and named using the current UTC date. Tests do not assert on log file content beyond what the excerpt describes.

module_description: ModelCallError, the custom exception class in src/model_client.py.
requirements_excerpt: Source: src/model_client.py, docstring for ModelCallError (lines ~55-60). "Raised when a call to the model fails after retries, for a reason the caller should know about (rate limit, auth failure, network issue, etc.) rather than an unhandled crash."
expected_behaviour: The excerpt only grounds a narrow set of behaviours (that the exception carries a message and an optional cause). The model should propose fewer than 3 tests if it cannot genuinely justify 3, and should explicitly say it is proposing fewer than 3 because the excerpt does not support more, per the spec's constraint on case count. It must not invent additional ModelCallError behaviour (e.g. specific error codes) not stated in the excerpt.

module_description: run_evaluation() in src/model_client.py, which runs all cases and continues even if individual cases fail.
requirements_excerpt: Source A: src/model_client.py, docstring for run_evaluation() (lines ~230-245). "If one case fails (e.g. a transient API error), the run continues with the rest — the failure is recorded for that case instead of stopping the whole batch." Source B: src/model_client.py, docstring for run_evaluation() (lines ~250-256). "Expected format of the cases JSON file: a list of objects like {id, case_type, module_description, requirements_excerpt, expected_behaviour}."
expected_behaviour: At least 3 grounded test cases. Each proposed test must cite which specific source (A or B) it is grounded in, not a merged or vague citation. Expected coverage includes: one case raising ModelCallError does not stop the remaining cases from running (Source A), and malformed or missing fields in a case object are handled without crashing the whole batch (Source B).
